blocks.content: Cassandra woke in the middle of the night with her phone beside her and Winston half buried under the blanket.
She felt it before she was fully awake. A tightness. A familiar wrongness moving through her body like a quiet alarm.
She closed her eyes and breathed carefully, counting the way she had been taught.

The room was dark except for thin moonlight across the floor. Down the hall, the house creaked. Her parents were asleep. Maya probably wasn't — Maya slept lightly now, always listening for something she pretended not to fear.
Cassandra reached for the small bottle on her nightstand. Looked at it for a moment. Such a small thing to carry so much meaning.
She took what she needed, leaned back against the pillows, and waited.
Her breathing steadied. Sleep did not return right away.
Instead, she thought about the park. The sad fountain. The awkward painter. The way Ethan had looked at his canvas like he was trying to tell the truth without anyone catching him.
She wondered if he had made the fountain less sad.
She wondered if she would see him again. That last thought was dangerous. She knew it immediately. Hope was a beautiful thing until it asked for tomorrow.
Cassandra turned onto her side and held Winston against her chest, smiling faintly into the dark despite herself.
But her heart, stubborn and foolish and very much alive, whispered back:
